newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht slides offshore on control lifting talk.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht slides offshore on control lifting talk.

text.p: The Thai baht fell sharply in early offshore trade on Friday on rumours that the central bank may remove its curb on offshore baht supply soon, dealers said.
"There is a rumour that the Bank of Thailand will lift the ban (on baht) for offshore parties. Somebody is spreading the rumour," a Singpore-based dealer told Reuters.
The baht fell to 24.550/24.650 to the dollar early in the offshore market from 24.100/24.200 late on Thursday.
Central bank officials are not immediately available for comment.

The Bank of Thailand has imposed what dealers called capital controls to cut off baht supply for offshore speculators since the latest market attack against the baht in mid-May. The two-tier offshore and onshore baht system has been adopted since then.
In the domestic market, the baht eased to 25.795/25.805 to the dollar from 25.770/25.790 late on Thursday in line with the dollar advance and strong commercial demand for the U.S. unit, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand set the baht/dollar midrate at 25.79 against 25.71 on Thursday.
"The dollar was still well bid here on commercial demand. The overall market remained quiet," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The talk also pushed the offshore baht/dollar one-month swap premiums down sharply to 80/90 satangs per dollar early from 110/130 late on Thursday, dealers said.
In the domestic market, the one-month swap premium fell to 14/19 satangs early against 16/20 late on Thursday.
The overnight interbank rate firmed slightly to 13.50-14.00 percent early from 13.00-13.50 late on Thursday on higher demand for funds, dealers said.
